newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UBS details results by division.
newsitem.headline: UBS details results by division.

text.p: Union Bank of Switzerland UBS released its results by division for 1996, providing for the first time what it called a breakdown of individual division results.
The figures were based on management accounting data.
The information was contained in a statement released to the press which followed a briefing for financial analysts earlier on Monday, UBS said.

It said that its private banking and institutional asset management division, with a pre-tax income of 1.91 billion Swiss francs, was the largest contributor to earnings "by a wide margin." The figure was based on 1.63 billion from private banking, and 280 million from institutional asset management.

"The bulk of private banking earnings are generated in Switzerland. UBS's strategic goals assign top priority to the expansion of asset management and private banking activities in and outside Switzerland," it said.

Its corporate and institutional finance division reported a 650 million Swiss franc loss. The figure contained a loss of 1.07 billion Swiss francs in domestic business and income of 420 million from non-Swiss operations.
"The figures show that, after the pre-emptive charge to 1996 earnings for potential future risks, there is considerable scope for an improvement in earnings," UBS said.

UBS said results in that division would be "additionally bolstered in future by more efficient process engineering, a firm commitment to risk-adjusted pricing and growing earnings streams from global investment banking".
Its trading and sales, risk management services division contributed 680 million Swiss francs to earnings in 1996, UBS said.

Earnings in that area would be enhanced by development of activities in emerging markets and "selective expansion of trading business in equity, fixed income, currency and commodities products as well as stabilisation in operational costs," it said.
Retail operations in Switzerland reported a loss of 130 million Swiss francs.
The figure reflected business including only customer accounts with assets of less than 100,000 Swiss francs, credits below 250,000 francs and mortgages of less than one million francs, it said.

"A modern customer-oriented range of services and distribution channels coupled with strict cost management will enable Swiss retail operations to make a positive contribution to group earnings in future," UBS said.

UBS already reported a group loss on 1996 results of 348 million Swiss francs on February 21. The results reflected one-time charges for credit risks to cover Swiss domestic loans totalling 4.4 billion Swiss francs which was charged to 1996 income.
